title: What is Lexcia?
content:
Lexcia is a new project building a conversational layer for content-rich websites. It helps visitors find and use the valuable knowledge an organization already has, through an assistant tailored to its website, brand and visitors. The exciting idea is to make that existing investment in knowledge easier to discover and use, without asking visitors to work through the website alone.

[About Lexcia](#about)

title: Why Lexcia?
content:
Organizations invest heavily in creating valuable knowledge and content, but much of that information remains buried inside their websites and difficult for users to access. Lexcia helps bridge that gap: visitors can ask in their own words and reach relevant information and pages while keeping the website in view.

[About Lexcia](#about)

title: What can Lexcia customize?
content:
Lexcia tailors the engine, content, interface, behavior, design and integration to each organization and website. The team works carefully and closely with customers to understand their needs, try the assistant together, and iteratively refine the design, answers and knowledge setup until they are happy with the agreed experience. Early customers help shape a new project around real needs.

[What we offer](#offer)

title: How does it work?
content:
Lexcia is designed to fit into the website a customer already has. In the proposed onboarding approach, Lexcia handles website mapping, content preparation, the searchable knowledge base, interface setup, testing and ongoing operation. The client typically only adds a lightweight JavaScript embed snippet to the existing website. The proposal aims to combine the interface and site-specific connection into one copy-paste snippet, making the customer’s part straightforward while the Lexcia team handles the work behind it. Hosting, monitoring, maintenance, analytics and ongoing improvements are part of the offering.

[How it works](#how)

title: Which websites is it for?
content:
Lexcia is for content-rich websites such as knowledge bases, guides, FAQs, directories and resource libraries, where visitors need help finding information.

[Who it’s for](#for)

title: Can I try Lexcia?
content:
The main current goal of Lexcia’s website is to invite prospective customers to a demo. The offered customer demo is a real working demonstration of how a chatbot could look and behave on the prospect’s own website, with an appropriate initial design and basic integration with their knowledge base. It gives the customer something concrete to try and discuss, so the team can refine the experience around their needs. The demo is free. This tailored customer demo is different from the assistant already on this landing page, which answers about Lexcia itself. No tailored customer demo is automatically created by entering a website address here. Schedule a demo currently opens a local form for preferred details and an event-summary draft; it does not check availability, book a meeting or send a request.

[Live demo](#demo)

title: How does pricing work?
content:
The planned model is a one-time setup fee plus a monthly subscription, with API usage billed separately. Approximate USD planning ranges for early customers: setup $810–$2,430 and monthly $80–$240. Future standard pricing after successful deployments and a proven process: setup $3,240–$8,090 and monthly $320–$810. Standard prices are future plans, not the current early-customer offer. These are estimates, not binding quotes; scope, traffic, integrations and content complexity affect the price. The subscription covers hosting, monitoring, maintenance, analytics and ongoing improvements. Early customers may receive further discounts for structured feedback, case studies and collaboration.

All displayed prices and estimates are in US dollars only.

Additional API-cost estimate: the October 11 architecture brief repriced a small development sample at GPT-6 Luna Standard rates of $0.10/million uncached input tokens and $0.50/million output tokens. The resulting averages were $1.82 per 1,000 answered questions (26 traces) and $3.05 per 1,000 tool-using questions (13 traces), or about $1.37–$2.29 for 750 questions/month. Each answered question may involve multiple provider calls. The sample was 32 requests / 85 calls, September 29–October 9, mostly GPT-5.6 Luna usage repriced; it is not a GPT-6 Luna benchmark, a live provider tariff, or a guaranteed bill. No cache savings assumed. Search, indexing, hosting, paid tools, added protection and support are excluded from the token estimate (some may be covered by the Lexcia subscription). Real costs depend on the chosen models, context, answer length and paid operations. Use this historical estimate as the current planning assumption requested by Asaf, not as measured cost for this landing-page assistant.
